loci.name: setfit-vs-llm-intent-with-uncertainty-routing
loci.one_line: Can a SetFit-first classifier with uncertainty-routed LLM fallback match native-LLM few-shot accuracy on noisy Twitter intents at a fraction of cost/latency?
opposing_positions: Small fine-tuned encoder first (SetFit/IntentBERT, 8-20 shots/class): within ~2pp of LLM F1, ~56x faster, ~28x cheaper to train; LLM only on uncertain routes
Native LLM few-shot (GPT-3.5/4 in-context): outright beats fine-tuned non-generative models on Banking77 with fewer examples, no gradient training, better wording variance
loci.rationale: Load-bearing for the re-engineering directive: picks the intent subsystem (model, training budget, latency envelope, reproducibility in 15 min) and defines baseline #1 vs #2. Twitter noise + small golden set (150-250) + cost constraints make the operating-point decision hinge on the routing threshold, MC-dropout/MaxProb signal, and OOS handling — all measurable in the harness.

loci.name: caged-judge-protocol-for-grounded-replies
loci.one_line: Which rubric-pinning + bias-mitigation + human-anchoring bundle makes an LLM judge trustworthy enough to score groundedness/actionability/tone on support replies?
opposing_positions: Judges usable: G-Eval CoT + form-filling reaches Spearman .514, output-based judges Pearson .81/.68, calibrated longitudinal tau .59-.68 — sufficient with rubric + mitigations + human anchor
Judges systematically biased: ~35% verdict flips on order swap, verbosity/self-preference persist, only 4/11 criteria human-equivalent; agreement must be demonstrated per deployment, never assumed
loci.rationale: The brief demands proof of trustworthiness via LLM-as-judge + human agreement. This locus decides the report's headline metric validity: judge-vs-generator separation, position-swap/verbosity controls, per-dimension kappa/tau targets, adjudication protocol, and what happens when agreement fails. Directly determines whether the eval harness verdicts survive audit.

loci.name: hybrid-retrieval-payoff-on-identifier-heavy-tweets
loci.one_line: How much does BM25+dense RRF/convex fusion + cross-encoder rerank beat pure dense on order-IDs, handles, error codes, and short noisy tweets — and at what latency cost?
opposing_positions: Hybrid+rerank is the production default: pure dense silently fails on exact identifiers/rare terms; RRF safe default, tuned alpha (+40 pairs) beats RRF; top-100 then cross-encoder top-5/10
Pure dense suffices at this scale: one good embedding model + metadata filtering covers paraphrase variance; second path doubles ingest/ops cost for unmeasured gain
loci.rationale: Decides the grounded-reply generator's evidence layer and baseline #2 design (pure-dense vs hybrid). Twitter traffic is identifier- and noise-heavy, so the margin must be measured on stratified/adversarial query splits (identifier vs semantic) with Recall@K/MRR/NDCG — not assumed. Latency budget (rerank ≤50 candidates, ~100-200ms) constrains the answer.

loci.name: escalation-calibration-under-shift
loci.one_line: What confidence signal + held-out threshold + risk-coverage reporting justifies auto-handle vs escalate, given MaxProb's cross-task robustness and over-abstention costs?
opposing_positions: Calibrated thresholding: temperature scaling (~31% ECE cut) + difficulty signals lift risk-coverage AUC 6-16% IID/OOD; threshold from calibration split is the production pattern
MaxProb sufficiency: across 17 datasets x IID/OOD/ADV no method consistently beats MaxProb; naive thresholds over-abstain, so learned modules must beat MaxProb on a temporal holdout or be dropped
loci.rationale: Decides the auto-handle/escalate decider — the safety-critical gate the audit must certify. Synthesis prescribes the experiment: MaxProb+calibration floor, risk-coverage/AURC reporting, temporal-split validation (leakage guard for Twitter time drift), and explicit false-auto-handle vs unnecessary-escalation cost trade-off that the report's trustworthiness claim rests on.
